review: Now listen. I have been in a church pew since 1962 and I stood in the second row of that choir for NINETEEN years before it dissolved, so when I tell you "Hammond Knows My Name" is right, understand what I am telling you. That is the instrument. Not a keyboard pretending. Somebody sat down at a real one and knew where to put their hands, and baby, I heard it in the first eight bars. I have played this album on my porch loud enough that Pearl came over from next door to find out what it was. Five stars and I do not hand those out.

review: Now listen, I am giving this four and I want to say WHY, because the singing is not the problem. The drums are programmed. I can hear it. There is a thing a real drummer does behind a choir where they breathe with the room and lean a hair late on the two and the four, and a machine will not do it because a machine is not listening to anybody. Everything else here is lovely. But my grandson runs our board and will not turn the tracks down and I have been having this argument for six years, and here it is again on a record. Somebody has to say it, so it is going to be me.
